pharm: Prodrug de-esterified to quinaprilat, which inhibits ACE, decreasing angiotensin II formation and aldosterone secretion and reducing peripheral vascular resistance.
quick: Hypertension: start 10-20 mg once daily; usual 20-80 mg/day, single or two divided doses
May be taken with or without food; high-fat meals can reduce absorption
Contraindicated; can cause fetal injury and death - stop as soon as pregnancy detected
Limited data; small amounts in milk - use with caution
Reduce initial dose; titrate by creatinine clearance
Conversion to active quinaprilat may be impaired; use with caution
Blood pressure, renal function, serum potassium, signs of angioedema
summary: Quinapril is an ACE inhibitor used to treat hypertension and, as an adjunct, heart failure. It is a prodrug converted to quinaprilat, which blocks conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, lowering vascular resistance and blood pressure. Key safety concerns are angioedema and anaphylactoid reactions, hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction (especially with renal artery stenosis or volume depletion), and a boxed warning for fetal toxicity requiring discontinuation when pregnancy is detected. It must not be combined with neprilysin inhibitors or with aliskiren in diabetics.
indications: Treatment of hypertension, alone or with other agents (e.g., thiazide diuretics)
Management of heart failure as adjunctive therapy when added to conventional therapy including diuretics and/or digitalis

dosage.d: Initial 10 or 20 mg once daily; usual 20, 40, or 80 mg/day as single or two divided doses
dosage.n: Adjust at intervals of at least 2 weeks based on peak/trough response

dosage.d: Initial 5 mg once daily, then titrate
dosage.n: Lower starting dose because of risk of symptomatic hypotension

dosage.d: Initial 5 mg twice daily; titrate to usual effective 20-40 mg/day in two divided doses
dosage.n: Watch for hypotension; observe after the first dose

dosage.d: CrCl >60: 10 mg; CrCl 30-60: 5 mg; CrCl 10-30: 2.5 mg (initial)
dosage.n: No data for CrCl <10; titrate cautiously

admin: Take at the same time each day, with or without food (avoid taking with high-fat meals which reduce absorption)
Correct volume/salt depletion before starting or start at a lower dose to limit first-dose hypotension
Do not start within 36 hours of switching to or from sacubitril/valsartan
Check renal function and potassium before and during therapy
moa: Quinapril is de-esterified to its active metabolite quinaprilat, which inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, a peptidyl dipeptidase that converts angiotensin I to the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II. Reduced angiotensin II decreases vasoconstriction and aldosterone secretion (lowering sodium and water retention) and increases plasma renin activity. ACE is identical to kininase II, so quinapril also reduces breakdown of bradykinin, which may contribute to vasodilation and to cough and angioedema. The net effect is reduced peripheral resistance and blood pressure.

absolute: History of angioedema related to previous ACE inhibitor therapy or hereditary/idiopathic angioedema
Concomitant use with a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril)
Co-administration with aliskiren in patients with diabetes
Pregnancy (drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause fetal injury/death)
relative: Volume or salt depletion / concurrent high-dose diuretics
Severe heart failure with marginal renal function
monitor: White blood cell count in collagen vascular/renal disease

preg: Boxed warning: drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus, particularly in the second and third trimesters (oligohydramnios, fetal renal failure, hypotension, skull hypoplasia, death). Discontinue quinapril as soon as pregnancy is detected and switch to an alternative.
lact: Quinapril is excreted in human milk in small amounts; because of the potential for adverse effects in the breastfed infant, use with caution and consider alternatives, especially in neonates and preterm infants.
renal: Quinaprilat is excreted renally and accumulates in renal impairment, so reduce the initial dose according to creatinine clearance and titrate carefully. ACE inhibition can reduce glomerular filtration in patients dependent on the renin-angiotensin system (bilateral renal artery stenosis, volume depletion); monitor creatinine and potassium and watch for acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia.
hepatic: Hepatic impairment may reduce de-esterification of quinapril to active quinaprilat, lowering efficacy; use with caution and monitor blood pressure response. Rarely, ACE inhibitors are associated with cholestatic hepatic injury - discontinue if marked transaminase rise or jaundice occurs.

major: Neprilysin inhibitors / sacubitril (contraindicated; increased angioedema risk)
Aliskiren in diabetics (contraindicated; renal impairment, hyperkalemia, hypotension)
moderate: NSAIDs (reduced antihypertensive effect and acute kidney injury, especially in elderly/volume-depleted)
mTOR inhibitors and DPP-4 inhibitors (increased angioedema risk)
minor: Tetracyclines (the magnesium in some quinapril tablets reduces tetracycline absorption)
interactions.food: High-fat meals can reduce absorption; otherwise may be taken with or without food.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause hyperkalemia and raised serum creatinine on laboratory testing.

rare: Anaphylactoid reactions (including during dialysis or LDL apheresis)

monitoring: Serum creatinine and potassium within 1-2 weeks of initiation/changes
Complete blood count in those with renal/collagen vascular disease
counsel: Stop the medicine and seek urgent care if you develop swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing
Tell your doctor immediately if you become or plan to become pregnant - this medicine can harm an unborn baby
A persistent dry cough can occur; report it as your doctor may switch you
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness, especially when starting
Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes unless advised; get blood tests as scheduled
pk: Blood-pressure lowering within about 1 hour of an oral dose
Quinaprilat peak plasma at about 2 hours; antihypertensive peak 2-6 hours
Effective accumulation half-life of quinaprilat about 3 hours (prolonged in renal impairment)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from moisture and light
pearls: Prodrug - converted to active quinaprilat; hepatic impairment may blunt efficacy
Angioedema can be life-threatening and is more common in Black patients; bradykinin-mediated
Watch creatinine and potassium after starting, especially with diuretics, NSAIDs or renal artery stenosis
Boxed fetal toxicity warning - stop immediately if pregnancy occurs
Tablet magnesium carbonate can reduce tetracycline absorption - separate dosing
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Overdose most likely manifests as severe hypotension. There is no specific antidote; treatment is supportive with intravenous normal saline to restore blood pressure and supine positioning. Monitor and correct electrolytes (hyperkalemia) and renal function. Hemodialysis removes quinaprilat to a limited extent and is not generally a primary treatment.
